sorted-pair.why: Sorted order tells you which pointer to move: too small, move left up; too big, move right down. O(n) time and O(1) space. A hash set is O(n) time but O(n) space; every pair is O(n²). A window is for contiguous ranges, not pairs.

palindrome.why: The pointers compare matching characters from both ends. "abca" fails at b vs c. For the empty string, right starts at -1, the loop never runs, and it returns true.

fixed-window.why: The window sums are 2+1+5 = 8, 1+5+1 = 7, 5+1+3 = 9 and 1+3+2 = 6. Sliding adds the new element and removes the one leaving, instead of re-adding all k.

window-fill.why: a[i] enters the window and a[i - k], the element k places back, leaves it.

move-zeros.why: Two pointers moving in the same direction (read and write) do it in one pass with O(1) space. A new array works but isn't in place. Sorting changes the other numbers' order, and counts lose it entirely.

window-negatives.why: The grow/shrink rule relies on sums only rising as the window grows. Negative numbers break that monotonicity; prefix sums with a sorted structure or a different technique is needed then.

pointers-cost.why: Every iteration moves one pointer one step closer to the other, so there are fewer than n iterations.
